faq.q: What is inside a smoke alarm?
faq.a: Most home smoke alarms have a small dark chamber with an infrared LED and a light sensor, a chip that watches the sensor, a loud piezo siren and a battery.
asks: How does a smoke alarm work inside?

faq.q: Why is the light sensor placed to one side?
faq.a: The sensor is set at an angle to the LED's beam, so in clean air no light reaches it. It only sees light when something in the chamber bounces the beam sideways.
asks: Why doesn't the sensor see the LED?

faq.q: How does smoke set off the alarm?
faq.a: Smoke particles scatter the LED's light in all directions, and some lands on the sensor. When the chip sees enough scattered light, it knows there is smoke.
asks: Why does burnt toast set off the alarm?

faq.q: Why is a smoke alarm so loud?
faq.a: It uses a piezo siren, a disc that flexes thousands of times a second. Alarms are made to reach at least about 85 decibels at 3 metres, loud enough to wake sleeping people.
asks: How loud is a smoke alarm?

faq.q: Why does my smoke alarm chirp?
faq.a: A short chirp every minute or so usually means the battery is low. It is the alarm asking for a new battery before it stops working.
asks: What does a beeping smoke alarm mean?

facts: Some smoke alarms use a different method: a tiny radioactive source makes the air in a chamber conduct, and smoke disrupts that current.
Smoke alarm sirens are designed to give at least about 85 decibels at 3 metres.

quiz.say: In an optical smoke alarm, what makes light reach the sensor?
quiz.show: In an optical smoke alarm, what makes light reach the sensor?
quiz.why: The sensor is out of line with the beam, so it only gets light when smoke particles bounce some sideways.

wrong.1: The LED stays the same; the sensor is not in its path anyway.
wrong.2: An optical alarm senses scattered light, not heat.
